Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mystery noun

also mysterious, mysteries, it’s a mystery, secret, puzzle (a mystery)

classical

rēs occulta

a hidden thing, something unknown

Plain prose says what is hidden or unknown: rēs occulta, rēs obscūra; “it’s a mystery to me” is nesciō quō pactō factum sit or mīrum est.

Other words

  • arcānum, arcānī n. — a secret, a mystery

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.85: quīcum arcāna, quīcum occulta omnia (Lewis & Short, s.v. arcānus)

    The neuter of arcānus, “kept close”: a secret, especially one kept or sacred; rare in Cicero.

  • mystērium, mystēriī n. — a secret rite; a secret; (Church) a mystery

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.18.1: epistulae nostrae tantum habent mystēriōrum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tusc. 4.55: rhētorum mystēria (Lewis & Short)

    The secret rites of Eleusis; in Cicero’s letters, jokingly, a secret; in Church Latin a truth beyond human understanding and a sacrament.

See also riddle, unclear.
